name: Havilah
overview: The Bible identifies Havilah both as a person and a place, demonstrating its significance in early biblical genealogy and geography. Havilah is named as a son of Cush and also as a son of Joktan, indicating distinct lineages (Genesis 10:7, 10:29). Geographically, Havilah refers to a region known for its gold, encompassed by the river Pison (Genesis 2:11), and is described as a district extending toward Shur near Egypt, east of Amalek (Genesis 25:18). These references highlight Havilah's role in the biblical narrative as both an ancestral figure and a notable location in the ancient world.
